question.text: The Byzantine capital was this city, which was renamed Istanbul after it fell to the Ottomans.
question.clue: Enrico Dandolo redirected the Fourth Crusade to attack this city, the location where Belisarius slaughtered a mob in the Hippodrome during the Nika Riots.

swap.text: Theodora may have influenced her husband to include women's rights in this legal code that is contained within the Corpus Juris Civilis . This legal code was created to specify the laws of the Byzantine Empire under its namesake emperor.
swap.clue: This work contains strikingly accurate transcription of quotes by Gaius and includes several writings by Ulpian as part of the Pandects, or Digest.

question.leadin: His campaigns against the Vandals and the Ostrogoths were much aided by his generals Narses and Belisarius.
question.text: Identify this ruler who built the Hagia Sophia and recodified laws in Corpus Juris Civilis.
question.answerHtml: Justinian I or Justinian the Great [prompt on partial answer]
question.answer: Justinian I or Justinian the Great
question.clue: Much of the history of this leader was recorded by Procopius , who traveled with his general Belisarius .

swap.text: This Byzantine Emperor tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Mediterranean, and this husband of Theodora was targeted in the Nika Riots.
swap.clue: The blues and the greens fought over a chariot race during this emperor's reign, which saw the creation of the Corpus Juris Civilis.

question.leadin: Name some things about the times when the use of religious images were opposed by both religious and Byzantine authority.
question.text: Name that time period during which depictions of religious figures was directly opposed by the leaders of the Eastern Church.
question.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

swap.text: Earlier, Belisarius put down this 532 uprising in Constantinople fought between the Blue and Green factions who had supported opposing sides of a chariot race.
swap.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

question.text: Name this event for which the engineer Orban designed a cannon known as "The Basilic" to destroy the Theodosian Walls.
question.answerHtml: Fall of Constantinople [accept answers generally describing a Siege of Constantinople; accept BUT DO NOT REVEAL answers indicating that Constantinople being is captured by the Ottomans; accept the end of the Byzantine Empire]

swap.text: Name this elite army unit that served as the personal bodyguards to the emperors of the Byzantine Empire.
swap.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

question.leadin: Fulk of Neuilly agitated for this event.

question.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

swap.text: According to George Akropolites, Tsar Kaloyan of Bulgaria made a skull cup out of the head of a ruler with this name. This name was shared by the first Latin Emperor of Constantinople as well as the Leper King of Jerusalem.

question.text: The "Eternal Peace" was signed after this Byzantine general defeated the Persians at the Battle of Dara. This general also conquered the Vandal kingdom and temporarily controlled Rome during the Gothic War.
question.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

swap.text: One exception to the rule about unblemished features was the second Byzantine ruler of this name, who took the throne after exile despite having his nose cut off. Another Byzantine ruler of this name put down the Nika Revolt.

question.text: Identify this emperor, who worked with his western counterpart Valentinian III and Antiochus Chuzon to assemble a code of law that formalized Christian law within the structure of the Roman Empire.
question.answerHtml: Theodosius II [prompt on Theodosius; do not accept or prompt on “Theodosius the Great”]

swap.leadin: Name some things about Christian Heresies before the Protestant Reformation.
swap.text: One heresy relies on the literal translation of the Ten Commandments,which forbids worshipping these "graven images." In the 8th century, the Eastern Church and Leo III banned the use of these images which often depict Jesus, Saints, and Angels.

question.leadin: Name some people whose writings serve as important primary sources about the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.
question.clue: This woman wrote admiringly of the manly traits of Empress Irene in her influential Byzantine history, The Alexiad.

swap.text: This porphyrogenitus Emperor became a legendary figure in Greek folklore called the "Marble King," who was saved from death by an angel who hid him in a cave. In non-deluded-Greek-nationalist-fantasyland, this man was killed by troops under Mehmet II.
swap.clue: In one battle, this man was relieved by ships commanded by Francesco Lecanella, who landed despite attacks from Admiral Baltoghlu.

question.text: The second ruler of this dynasty, Leo VI the Wise, prescribed harsh punishments for counterfeiting alchemists in his Book of the Eparch. Leo completed the Basilika law code named after the founder of this dynasty, Basil I.
question.clue: Chief military figures from this period include Nicephorus Phocas and an Armenian usurper, John Tzimisces, though its most notable battlefield accomplishment may have come against the army of Tsar Samuel.
